paper.title: LADDER: Self-Improving LLMs Through Recursive Problem Decomposition
paper.central_claim: Recursive easier integral generation supplies a verified curriculum for GRPO weight training; problem-specific test-time RL further improves integration accuracy.

provenance.notes: Runtime context names gpt-6.1-sol; independently exported actual-model receipt/session unavailable. No probing.

sections_read: Full abstract, §§1–6, Algorithms 1–2, GRPO equations and Appendix: MIT Integration Bee Failed Questions
materials.notes: Article footer carries August 24, 2026 while arXiv version header is v3 05 Mar 2025; review is bound to supplied hash, no version correction inferred.

evidence.quote: Second, we perform the reinforcement learning protocol
evidence.support_explanation: LADDER trains model weights on generated integral variants, rather than editing retained harness state.

evidence.quote: the model is rolled back to its original parameters for the next test question.
evidence.support_explanation: TTRL changes weights temporarily per problem; no cross-task harness persistence demonstrated.

evidence.quote: This transformation library served as a foundation for guiding variant generation.
evidence.support_explanation: Library is an initial generation aid, not an outcome-updated evaluated non-weight learning artifact.

evidence.quote: The problem is considered "solved" if the model produces a correct solution at any point during this process
evidence.support_explanation: TTRL outcome includes checker-selected attempts; scope decision does not depend on headline performance.

evidence.quote: LADDER achieved 82% accuracy on the test set
evidence.support_explanation: Reported improvement concerns the weight-trained solver.

evidence.quote: For our Llama experiments, approximately 8% of generated variants were effectively unsolvable
evidence.support_explanation: Generation failure is acknowledged; does not establish non-weight adaptation.

evidence.quote: While our current approach uses static parameters for variant generation
evidence.support_explanation: Adaptive generation-policy editing is future work, not current retained harness improvement.

signatures.information: Seed integral problems and numerical correctness verifier
signatures.operation: Generate recursive simpler/equivalent variants; train solver via GRPO accuracy/format rewards.
signatures.conditions: Numerically verifiable answers, variants accessible within model competence
signatures.selection_rule: GRPO group-relative reward updates policy parameters
signatures.persistence: Persistent model weights, not prompt/tool/workflow/memory edits
signatures.claimed_effect: Llama 3B 1% to 82%; Qwen 7B 50% to 73% on MIT
signatures.failure_boundary: Variant difficulty drift, checker error, domain restriction

signatures.information: Test integral and checker; variants of that test problem
signatures.operation: Generate variants, run up to 100 GRPO steps and seek a correct target response.
signatures.output: Problem-specific adapted model and checked answer
signatures.selection_rule: Success at any point; reset weights for next test problem
signatures.selection_data: Test-specific variant tree and target verification
signatures.persistence: No retained cross-problem update; weights reset. Transformation generator/library is not feedback-edited.
signatures.failure_boundary: Not an oracle-free single-pass comparison and no persistent harness learning

gap.author_gap: RL stalls on problems beyond model capability without a difficulty gradient.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete curriculum/weight-learning problem, not a retained harness bottleneck in present scope.
gap.closest_adjacent: Verified curriculum and test-time weight adaptation
gap.residue: Recursive easier-variant curriculum and targeted problem-level RL
gap.stakes: Weak solvers lack positive rewards on hard integration tasks
gap.remaining_gap: Adaptive difficulty policy is future work; no evaluated retained non-weight artifact.

claims.text: LADDER/TTRL improve integration performance through recursive curriculum and RL.
claims.selection_vs_test: LADDER train/test split; TTRL trains on variants of test item and checks target during adaptation.
claims.result/denominator: Reported 82% of 100 undergraduate test questions; 73%/90% MIT 20-question exam.
counterevidence: Does not measure retained non-weight harness improvement.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Weight-adaptation study outside this radar’s frozen scope; reported performance not scored here.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Authors report weight-learning gains from verified curricula; no evaluated retained non-weight improvement object.
unresolved: Out-of-scope disposition is not an assessment that the mathematical training results are false.

reason: Frozen A3 and EVIDENCE scope: evaluated adaptation and durable LADDER output are solver weights. The generation library is a fixed aid rather than an execution-feedback-updated retained harness object; TTRL resets weights after each question.
rationale: 递归题目生成服务于 GRPO 权重训练；TTRL 每题训练后回滚参数。没有被评价的留存非权重组件，依冻结 A3 排除，不以低分代替范围裁定。
